You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer runtime-linux):
- file: .gitignore:12
- category: hygiene
- title: rt_linux fixture droppings (rt_linux_file_test.tmp, rt_linux_mmap_test.tmp) land untracked at repo root
- detail: git status shows untracked rt_linux_file_test.tmp and rt_linux_mmap_test.tmp at the repo root. Their origin is proven: tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.c line 31 and rt_linux_mmap.c line 39 open the relative paths "rt_linux_file_test.tmp"/"rt_linux_mmap_test.tmp", and tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_file.sh runs the simulator with `cd "$ROOT"` (line 68), so the HTIF host-side relay resolves the guest's relative path against the repo root and creates the files there. .gitignore already has a section for exactly this pattern ('# Notebook/tutorial scratch at repo root', lines 12-20 with /hello.c etc.) but has no entry for these; every vlinux file-io test run re-dirties the working tree. Fix: add `/rt_linux_*.tmp` to that section.
- claimed safety: gitignore-only change; no build, test, or runtime input reads .gitignore, so nothing can change behavior. The files are regenerated by the tests either way.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. - verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# U5 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): the File I/O syscall set (openat,
3	# close, read, pread64, lseek, fstat, fstatat, statx, faccessat, getcwd,
4	# readlinkat, getdents64) bridged onto the existing HTIF window ops.
5	#
6	# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.c: fopen/fwrite/fclose then fopen/fseek/
7	# ftell/fread/fclose (ordinary glibc stdio -- openat/write/close/lseek/
8	# read/fstat), then direct syscall() probes for the rest of the set.
9	# Deterministic output (fixed payload, no printed pointers/times), so the
10	# test matches it exactly on both legs.
11	#
12	# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
13	# as test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh.
14	set -uo pipefail
15	
16	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
17	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
18	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
19	
20	TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
21	[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
22	export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"
23	
24	LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
25	if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
26	  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
27	  exit 0
28	fi
29	
30	bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
31	BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
32	[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"
33	
34	make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
35	[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"
36	
37	make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_file.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
38	  || fail "file-io fixture build failed"
39	APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_file.elf"
40	[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"
41	
42	SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
43	[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
44	
45	EXPECT_LINES=(
46	  "FILEIO: stdio size=37 ok"
47	  "FILEIO: fstat size=37 ok"
48	  "FILEIO: pread64 ok"
49	  "FILEIO: fstatat ok"
50	  "FILEIO: faccessat ok"
51	  "FILEIO: readlinkat correctly EINVAL"
52	  "file io ok"
53	)
54	
55	check_leg() {
56	  local label="$1" rc="$2" out="$3"
57	  local line
58	  for line in "${EXPECT_LINES[@]}"; do
59	    printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$line" \
60	      || fail "$label: missing '$line' in: $out"
61	  done
62	  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "$label: exit $rc != 0: $out"
63	  ok "$label: openat/close/read/pread64/lseek/fstat/fstatat/faccessat/getcwd/readlinkat/getdents64 all correct"
64	}
65	
66	# 1. fast leg. Runs from the driver's own workdir -- the tmp file lands
67	#    there, same convention as tests/vplat's vplat_file.c.
68	out=$(cd "$ROOT" && timeout 30 "$BIN" run --mode fast --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1); rc=$?
69	check_leg "fast" "$rc" "$out"
70	
71	# 2. cycle leg: the SAME staged vlinux-run.elf, run directly (U1's
72	#    dual-engine pattern). The dominant cost is glibc's own startup
73	#    machinery (TLS setup, riscv_hwprobe loop, ...), the SAME cost U4
74	#    already measured at ~7 minutes wall-clock on this host's vsim
75	#    (~8 kHz) -- the file I/O syscalls this feature adds are cheap by
76	#    comparison, so the same 600s timeout applies, not a shorter one.
77	vlinux_run=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -oE '/[^ ]*/vlinux-run\.elf' | head -1)
78	[ -n "$vlinux_run" ] && [ -f "$vlinux_run" ] \
79	  || fail "staged vlinux-run.elf not found on disk: $vlinux_run"
80	
81	out=$(timeout 600 "$SIM" "$vlinux_run" 2>&1); rc=$?
82	check_leg "cycle" "$rc" "$out"
83
